In response to stress or vascular injury, contractile VSMCs can switch to a less differenti-
ated state (synthetic phenotype) to acquire the proliferative, migratory, and synthetic capabilities for
tissue reparation.
Imbalances in VSMCs phenotypic switching can result in a variety of cardiovascular
diseases, including atherosclerosis, in-stent restenosis, aortic aneurysms, and vascular calcification.
It
is very important to identify the molecular mechanisms regulating VSMCs phenotypic switching
to prevent and treat cardiovascular diseases with high morbidity and mortality.
